sectionTitles.preservation: Drying food for storage and travel

name: Sietch production and domestic life
notes: Native graphics remain placeholders. Focused regression checks do not establish campaign balance.

Native construction costs, recipe gates and expedition scale are audited in Docs/INDUSTRY_BALANCE_20261019.md. The industry entity records are bounded patch-authored views; Core costs and inherited statistics are not resolved there.

sections.body: Open Options, then Mod options, Sands of Arrakis and Open the sietch field guide. The guide can be reopened after the arrival letter is dismissed. It covers the first water and food supply, cooling, textiles, safe rock, shield combat, medical care and physical trade. Scroll to reach the later sections.
sections.title: Finding the sietch field guide

sections.body:
The Fremen opening includes 1,150 steel, a finite reserve for the first buildings and repairs. Install the carried condenser and protect food in an enclosed, roofed pantry before committing to large garden walls. Use a capable constructor: failed construction spends real materials.

Windtraps, irrigated food and fiber beds, passive cooling and a small solar-and-storage cooking grid form the early supply loop. A hand tailoring station weaves eight desert fibers into six Cloth with 600 base work. Keep cloth for equipment such as cooler pads, and preserve emergency fuel while the grid comes online. Opening food supply remains under review in the alpha.
sections.title: The first workshops

sections.body:
The desert can overwhelm an undersized room cooler. Thick mountain rock buffers heat and cold, while surface shelters need more active cooling. Walls, a complete roof and a closed entrance matter; an open canopy still shares the outside air. Keep sustained cooking and workshop heat away from sleeping quarters.

For a fully enclosed seven-by-seven surface room, controlled tests held the settled temperature below 29 C with two passive water coolers at 60 C outside, or two powered water coolers at 75 C. Larger halls need more capacity. The cooler inspector shows the actual room size, temperature and target; a lower target does not make the machine stronger. These reference tests include a small internal heat load and regular door traffic, but do not guarantee every layout or weather setting.

Keep filled passive backups and a hauler available through sleep shifts. Tanks refill only when empty, and a stockpile cannot cool a room while its reservoir is dry. In the seven-by-seven 60 C reference room, two passive backups held a six-hour power interruption below 32 C; deep-rock shelter needed only one backup to stay near 30 C.

A sealed climate cooler uses electricity and needs its red exhaust side open to outdoor air. Very hot exhaust reduces its output. Desert freezers need several units and a temperature buffer below freezing; they should be closed, separated from hot equipment and checked through the hottest part of the day. Water-fed coolers are for occupied rooms and cannot refrigerate food.

A full water store cannot help a cooler until someone reaches it. In the tested 49-cell surface refuge at 60 C outside, two passive primary coolers overheated during a one-hour refill delay; one filled passive backup set to 30 C kept the room below 32 C. Three- and six-hour delays needed two backups in that layout. Thick stone greatly reduced the same demand. These are reference layouts, not guarantees for every room.

Cooling needs attention appears when an enabled water cooler serves a room at least 35 C and more than 5 C above its effective target. Check the water reserve, power, breakdowns, walls, roof and doors. A hot newly built room may simply be cooling down; sustained heat calls for more capacity or a smaller refuge. The warning clears as the room cools and ignores coolers deliberately switched off. Pawn tolerances still differ.
sections.title: Keeping the sietch cool

sections.body:
Desert fuel processing follows sietch electrics. The processor draws 170 W and turns 3.5 nutrition of pundi rice, Gift to the Thirsty or Fremen wheat into 35 Chemfuel with 2,500 base work. Irrigation has already paid the crops’ water cost; refining adds no second water charge.

Food and fuel compete for the same harvest. Fiber, cloth, medicine, spice, meals and wood cannot be used in this bill. Use grid cooking and glowglobes for routine work where possible; finite smuggler fuel stocks offer another recovery route.
sections.title: Food crops and Chemfuel

sections.body:
Hooded sietch lamps and recessed wall lamps can light rooms without grid power. Both use steel construction and begin empty, requiring hauled Chemfuel. Their base burn is two fuel per day, with capacities of twenty and fifteen respectively; environment and difficulty can alter consumption.

These lamps provide light during an outage, but they add a continuing fuel demand. Fuel already held by an older saved lamp remains in its reserve.
sections.title: Flame lighting

sections.body:
A component workshop costs 200 steel, twelve industrial components and two advanced components. Its component bill requires Crafting 8, twelve steel and 5,000 base work for one finished component. The advanced bill uses one component, twenty steel, ten plasteel and three gold, with Crafting 8 and 10,000 base work.

Smuggler settlements sell finite stocks of components and precision materials to help establish the workshop. Later surveys and expeditions can renew supply, while trade avoids the need to staff and transport a mining party.
sections.title: Making industrial components

sections.body:
Early research and stonecutting can proceed without electricity. The sietch study desk needs 25 steel and 75 compatible material, including local stone. The stonecutting table needs 30 steel fittings and 75 metal or wood. These are fixed fittings in addition to the selected construction material.

Powered tailoring costs 50 steel, two components and 75 material, and draws 120 W. Metalworking costs 100 steel and three components at 210 W; the precision workshop costs 150 steel and five components at 350 W; the salvage smelter costs 170 steel and two components at 700 W.

A House research workstation needs 100 steel, ten components and 150 metallic construction material, drawing 250 W. Linked analytical instruments cost 40 steel, 50 plasteel, twenty gold and eight components at 200 W, adding 10% research speed and enabling projects that require them. An unpowered tool rack costs 200 steel and adds 6% work speed to eligible linked benches; at most two apply per bench.
sections.title: Benches, research and power demand

sections.body:
Desert mineral survey research has 2,000 base research points and requires microelectronics, machining and a powered House research workstation. The survey console costs 200 steel, six components and two advanced components and draws 700 W. An operator must work at it outdoors.

Choose steel, gold, plasteel, uranium or industrial components. Finds average four operator research-work days apart, with a guarantee after eight; skill, interruptions and power change the elapsed calendar time. Repeated surveys can locate new finite deposits.

A caravan must reach the site, mine the resource and bring it home. The initial quest allows thirty days to reach it. Once a site map is generated, its separate eleven-day exit countdown applies. Opposition depends on an eligible enemy, so some sites are unguarded. The console supplies a destination, not delivered cargo.
sections.title: Surveying distant deposits

sections.body:
Sietch fiber and weaving provide dependable local Cloth. Hunting supported animals or butchering kulon can supply leather, but kulon produce no wool. Smugglers sell limited stocks of plain leather, wool, synthread, devilstrand fabric and hyperweave.

These fabrics remain paid imports. Plan garment production around what is actually in storage rather than assuming the next trader will carry a particular material.
sections.title: Local cloth and imported fabric

sections.body:
Powered sietch cultivation provides troughs with 2.8 fertility and 70 W pumps. Each starts with an empty two-ration reserve and accepts reclaimed Arrakis crops. Water is consumed as growth occurs; faster production does not make a full harvest cheaper in water.

Cultivation lights draw 2,900 W while on and switch off for plant rest. A power failure can kill trough crops. Size generation and storage for the lighting load, keep irrigation supplied and maintain a suitable room temperature.
sections.title: Powered cultivation

sections.body:
Powered cooking stations support vegetarian fine and lavish meals, including bulk bills. Pundi rice, Gift to the Thirsty and Fremen wheat provide the edible staples, allowing richer meals without a livestock industry. Cooking skill, work and ingredient nutrition requirements still apply.

Tea, pressed trail rations, journey rations and fresh ration dispensing have separate recipes. Their water and food costs should be planned separately from ordinary meals.
sections.title: Meals for an established sietch

sections.body:
After pressed trail rations research, a cook can use a preservation crock to turn twenty edible crop units into sixteen dried staples with 1,500 base work. The batch converts 1.0 nutrition into 0.8, losing a fifth during trimming and drying. It needs no added water, salt, fuel or electricity.

Dried staples last seventy days at room temperature. Refrigeration slows rot and freezing stops it, while outdoor exposure still causes deterioration. At 10°C and above, the underlying rot rate is already at its maximum. Keep the finished stores under cover.
sections.title: Drying food for storage and travel

sections.body:
The ornamental planter grows a dedicated windcup cultivar. It begins with an empty one-ration reserve; establishing the plant consumes half a ration. A mature plant has no ongoing growth-based water charge.

This is decoration for the sietch rather than a harvest bed. It produces no food, fiber or medicine and does not replace the wild windcup used for fiber collection.
sections.title: A little green indoors

sections.body:
Sleeping frames and rolls, eating tables, seats and gathering places make an enclosed shelter into a home. Assignment, comfort, quality and room arrangement still govern how people use them. Doors need proper support, and powered bulkheads need a functioning grid.

Supply racks use storage filters, priorities and triple-stack capacity, but do not refrigerate their contents. Archive cabinets hold physical books and support nearby academic work. Use bill suspension, work priorities, areas and schedules to keep supplies moving between rooms. Stone, metal and local fabric can substitute for scarce wood where a building permits them.
sections.title: Rooms, stores and daily work

sections.body:
Desert strategy tables and smugglers card tables provide cerebral recreation, while House leisure tables offer a dexterity game. Put seats beside games that require them. Card and leisure tables use steel fittings while retaining their Cloth cost.

Story projectors and House panels need current and clear viewing areas. The assembly projection wall requires projection-panel research and component fabrication. Imported gold is needed for the Great House sleeping dais and ceremonial doorways. Memorial caskets provide burial; perform any chosen deathstill reclamation before interment.
sections.title: Games and House furnishings

sections.body:
Jade arrives through paid smuggler imports: caravans carry 20–40 per stock generation and settlements 40–80. At a base value of five and mass of 0.5 kg each, a fifty-Jade small sculpture may require more than one purchase. Jade is not an industrial survey target.

Throwing-spear bundles use seventy steel, Crafting 3 and 7,000 work, retaining repeated throwing without separate ammunition. Tool racks support at most two facility benefits per eligible bench. Material access, available money and work time still govern how quickly a colony can equip its workshops.
sections.title: Ornament and workshop equipment

sections.body:
Smuggler caravans and House caravans or settlements carry 80–160 alfalfa per stock generation; smuggler settlements carry 160–200. These finite stocks can support livestock until irrigated fodder is established. Restocking follows normal trade intervals.

A smuggler settlement also offers one desert observation scope and one physical novel per stock generation. They must be purchased, hauled home and placed for use; neither is an automatic starting gift.
sections.title: Buying provisions and leisure goods

sections.body:
Sietch surgical beds and powered support consoles improve treatment and surgery. Field prosthetics research allows mechanical arms and legs to be produced at the precision workshop. More advanced replacements remain an offworld expense.

Smuggler bases sell Imperial cardiac prostheses, hearing restoration implants, Suk trauma kits, House precision arms and legs, and optical implants. Surgery consumes the actual part and medicine and still carries risk. An imported replacement cannot be installed merely because its research or trade route is known.
sections.title: Care and imported replacements

sections.body:
Evening primrose provides herbal-tier desert medicinals from reclaimed irrigated beds or sparse wild plants. Cultivation requires Plants 8. The packets have 60% potency and a 70% treatment-quality cap. Offworld medical kits and limited Suk trauma kits must be bought; local industrial medicine synthesis is unavailable.

A field arm or leg costs forty steel and four components and requires Crafting 5 at the precision workshop. Installation needs Medicine 4, two eligible medicine items and the physical part. Surgical failure and reduced replacement efficiency remain possible.

An adjacent surgical support console draws 80 W and must be linked to a bed; at most one console benefit applies per bed. Cryptosleep and stasis are outside the supported alpha.
sections.title: Medicinals and field surgery

sections.body:
Six working crops grow in reclaimed beds or powered troughs: pundi rice, Gift to the Thirsty, Fremen wheat, alfalfa, sietch fiber and evening primrose. On Arrakis and Fremen maps they require compatible irrigation-equipped growers. A fertile ground zone does not provide a water-free farming route.

Ornamental windcup uses its own planter. Wild hookwood supplies scarce timber. Kulon, Muad’Dib and sand terrapins make up the supported fauna; local milk, wool, trained companions and a wider crop roster remain outside this alpha. Growing on unrelated non-Fremen worlds is unchanged.
sections.title: Crops and animals

sections.body:
Deep-desert rigs provide a separate steel route using finite underground ore: at most six structural-metal deposits per map at one-quarter the usual size. A working rig emits Maker vibration on exposed sand. Remote surveys instead send caravans to industrial deposits elsewhere.

Components and advanced components have local fabrication bills, but their inputs still need to be acquired. Trade offers supplies without a mining expedition; it does not guarantee daily income or a particular stock roll. Long-term production balance and some final art and sound remain in development.
sections.title: Limits of local industry

summary: A working sietch turns water, reclaimed soil and scarce materials into food, clothing and shelter. Trade and expeditions supply the precision goods its workshops cannot yet produce.
